section: execution_count — 148.04-162.81 s (beats 320-352, bars 80-87): twelve EXECUTION shouts (lines 86-97), six counts (lines 98-103), final shout (line 104). Files: src/scenes/11_execution.js, src/scenes/11_count.js, docs/v3/errors.json
summary: v3 plays the twelve shouts as twelve presses of Regenerate on the user's first question: 12 hard-cut shots of 2 beats each (exec-01..12), every one a different failed answer with its own composition, its own micro-copy and one of three full-field palettes (dark error, flat red, cream). The only constants are a 204x52 px attempt pager in the top-right corner and the user's question bubble; the sung word changes place, size (40-349 px), typeface and colour in every shot, and 7 of the 12 shots carry the old anime illustrations (three of them untreated, in full colour). The counting is six full-frame dark cards (huge orange serif numeral in the centre, the number word in its own script on one side, a 'Reply language' chip on the other, chat-style chrome top and bottom), each arriving by a different 0.10-0.12 s wipe, then the six cards fold into tiles inside the chat window and the last shout is a serif bubble that hits the window edge and gets the film's first 'Reached no one' badge. Musically this is the most rigid passage of the song: 12 identical 2-beat cells at flat loudness, then a stop-time bar where the voice counts on six consecutive beats, then one last shout over near-silence into the loudest downbeat (162.81). Measured against the audio, the 12 shot cuts sit exactly on the sung onsets, but the six count cards and the end of exec-12 are half a beat early (v3 followed the LRC, which runs 0.2-0.5 s early here). No code, loop or run counter is shown anywhere, so the passage reads as twelve unrelated slides followed by a well-built counting gag in chat-UI skin.

diagnosis:
What the frames show, against what the music does.

1) Twelve slides, not one event. Looking at one frame per beat, nothing carries across any of the 12 cuts except a 204x52 px pager (28 px text) in the corner and a small question bubble that itself moves and changes size. The sung word, which is the only thing the ear hears, is re-placed every 0.92 s: low centre 92 px, macro 190 px, full-bleed 349 px, bottom-left 104 px, centre 250 px sans, 24 copies at 40 px, upper-left 98 px, corner 70 px, caption 66 px, bottom-right 78 px, right-of-centre 150 px split, left 300 px serif. In shots 2, 8, 9 and 10 it is not even the subject of the frame. The eye has to find it again each time, so every cut feels like being thrown into an unrelated picture: this is the 'forced transition' the director describes. All twelve enters are plain cuts (`enter: { type: 'cut' }`), with a 2.2 % zoom kick on dark shots only, so some cuts pop and others do not.

2) Three full-field palettes flip the whole screen. Field order is D D R D C D R D D C D R, then dark for the count. Measured mean relative luminance per shot: 0.013, 0.03, 0.18, 0.04, 0.73, 0.02-0.06, 0.16, 0.018, 0.021, 0.58, 0.10, 0.16-0.20, count 0.04-0.06. After 22 s of dark red build-up, the cream shots (151.73 and 156.34) are near-white screens that look like another film, and the red posters change the meaning of the colours: in errRed the role `me` is pale pink (#ffd9c6) and `err` is charcoal, in errCream `me` is brown, so 'orange = me, red = error' does not hold in 5 of 12 shots.

3) Each shot is a micro-story that cannot be read. The concept (attempt n of 12, each fails differently) lives in 24-30 px mono labels, the second of which appears on beat 2 (0.41 s after the cut) and is gone 0.5 s later. Without reading them the frames have no common subject, so the variety looks arbitrary. Nothing accumulates: shot 12 is not visibly 'more' than shot 1.

4) The illustrations. 7 of 12 shots use the anime art; exec-06 (24 thumbnails), exec-07 (full height on red) and exec-11 (banded) show it untreated with painted shading, gold detail and four or five colours against flat three-colour UI. exec-07 and exec-12 are figure-on-poster layouts with no relation to the surrounding film; in exec-12 the duotone turns her grey-sepia on red. The new three-ink cut-paper busts (orange / cream / near-black, transparent, 1086x1448 or 1254x1254) are busts, not full figures, so none of the current full-height placements can simply be re-pointed at them.

5) The music says 'loop', the picture says 'variety'. The audio is 12 identical 2-beat cells (same breakbeat cell, flat RMS 0.49-0.54, four even eighth-note syllables on N, N+0.5, N+1, N+1.5; onset autocorrelation 0.47 at 2 beats versus 0.13 at other lags). The picture answers the most mechanical passage of the song with its most heterogeneous one, and shows no code, no loop, no run counter: 'execution' is treated as a chat reply. Inside a cell the image moves only on the cut; the three later syllables have no visual counterpart. The one shot that is about repetition (exec-06: a grid filling in one beat, 'n of 24 identical', nobody presses Stop) is also the one that reads fastest, which supports the director's own suggestion.

6) Sync slip at the join. The LRC is 0.19-0.52 s early and irregular in this passage. v3 ignored it for the shouts (cuts at Bt(320+2i), verified on the sung onsets within 0.02 s) but followed it for the count: cards cut at beats 343.5...348.5 while the voice counts on beats 344...349 (voiced-harmonic onsets at 159.12, 159.59, 160.03, 160.51, 160.94, 161.43, each about 0.17 s long at one pitch near 294 Hz). So exec-12 loses its last half beat, every numeral arrives in a gap, and the sung number coincides with a 23 px 'no reply' label instead of with the numeral. The director did not name this, but it is part of why the counting, though 'roughly as imagined', does not punch.

7) The counting cards are sound in layout and wrong in skin. What works: one huge centred numeral per count on a dark page, the number word in its own script alternating sides, a slight growth card to card. What ties it to the old concept: the rounded card frame, 'Trying another language' + retry icon, 'attempt n of 6', the 'Reply language' pill with chevron, the red 'no reply' tag, the tab strip of six language names with strike-throughs, the sunburst dial, and the fold into tiles inside the chat window with a message bubble and delivery badge. Nearly all of that text is 22-24 px and on screen for 0.46 s. Six different wipe mechanisms in 2.8 s repeat the 'variety for its own sake' problem in small, though the constant layout hides it.

8) Weak launch into chorus 2. From 162.30 to 162.81 the frame is static while the last shout finishes over a bass swell and the full band re-enters at 162.81 with double the high-band energy. The director wants chorus 2 to be the strongest, glitch-ridden part; the section currently hands it a quiet, tidy chat window.
keep: Cut grid of the twelve shouts: `cut(i) = Bt(320 + 2 * i)` (148.04 + 0.923 s x i). Verified on the sung onsets; the regularity is the point of the passage.

exec-03's treatment of the word: system mono 800, full-bleed (349 px, 1884 px wide), held still, a rule drawing under it in 0.3 s. It is the natural seed of a code-style look (but on the dark field, not red).

exec-06's loop mechanism: a grid that fills cell by cell inside one beat, a live counter ('n of 24 identical'), a meter that runs to the end, a Stop control nobody presses. Keep the mechanism, drop the thumbnails.
The run counter idea of the pager (n/12 plus twelve ticks that are used up, `pager()` / `PG`), as an iteration counter; it must become a primary element instead of a 204x52 px corner chip.
The typographic arc: the word is mono (a command) for eleven shouts and becomes her serif on the twelfth (exec-12). Worth keeping as the one planned change inside the loop.

Deterministic tear looks that match the approved glitch of section 9: exec-11's word split across a seam with halves 16 px apart and bands sliding to rest in 0.3 s; exec-07's three-plate misregistration of outlines; exec-02's `wall()` of the word as outlined texture and its type / delete / retype gesture.

Count layout: one full-frame dark card per number; Arabic numeral in Source Serif 900 centred at (960, 540), size 820 + 30 x i px, slow 3.5 % push while it holds, outline echo offset 2.2 %; number word in its own script, cream, 156-216 px, alternating sides at x 385 / 1535.
CJK pipeline: config.json fonts.cjk roles krSerif / krSans / tcSerif / tcSans with only the needed glyphs preloaded; `ctx.text` reports any other glyph instead of falling back.
Count stays dark in every frame with reduced bloom (`GLOW = 0.3`); each in-canvas wipe is finished within 0.12 s; the helpers `masked`, `wedges`, `blinds`, `interleave` are reusable and safe.
Final shout timing: impact at `HIT = Bt(350)` = 161.88 on the sung onset, with squash and a red edge line; the word in her serif (continuity with exec-12).
Dark error palette as the base state (bg #1d1413, orange #d97757 / #ee8f66, cream #faf9f5, red #f5506f): it is the state both neighbours (err-breath before, cx-give after) are in.
Everything is a pure function of t with seeded randomness (`rand(key, i)`), nothing re-seeded per frame: required for both determinism and flash safety.
problems: 12 unrelated compositions joined by 12 hard cuts every 0.92 s; no shared anchor, motion or shape across any cut; zoom kick on 7 dark shots only.

The sung word changes position, size (40 to 349 px), typeface (mono x10, sans x1, serif x1) and colour in every shot; in exec-02 (beat 1), exec-08, exec-09 and exec-10 it is not the subject of the frame on the hit.

Three full-field palettes in the order D D R D C D R D D C D R: whole-frame luminance jumps 0.05 to 0.73 to 0.02 around exec-05 and 0.02 to 0.58 to 0.10 around exec-10; red and cream palettes remap `me` and `err`, breaking the film's colour semantics in 5 shots.

Old anime illustrations in 7 of 12 shots (exec-04, 05, 06, 07, 09, 11, 12), untreated full colour in exec-06, exec-07 and exec-11; they also rely on full-figure art, which the new silhouette set (busts) does not provide.
The 'twelve regenerate attempts' story is carried by 24-30 px mono micro-copy visible for about 0.5 s and by a corner pager; unreadable at speed, so the variety looks arbitrary.
No code, no loop, no execution in the programming sense; the most mechanical 11 s of audio get the most heterogeneous pictures; no accumulation or escalation from shout 1 to 12.
No visual accents inside a 2-beat cell although the word is four even syllables (N, N+0.5, N+1, N+1.5).
exec-12 is 1.5 beats and is cut at 158.88 under its last syllable.

Count cards cut on beats 343.5...348.5 (158.88, 159.34, 159.81, 160.27, 160.73, 161.19) while the numbers are sung on beats 344...349 (159.11, 159.58, 160.04, 160.50, 160.96, 161.42): every numeral and every wipe lands in a gap half a beat early.

Count skin is chat UI throughout (card frame, 'Trying another language', 'attempt n of 6', 'Reply language' chip, 'no reply' tag, struck-through language tabs, sunburst dial); most of that copy is 22-24 px for 0.46 s; six different wipe mechanisms in 2.8 s.

count-out returns to the chat window (tiles, bubble, 'Reached no one' badge) and holds a static frame from 162.30 to 162.81, a weak lead-in to the loudest downbeat and to a chorus the director wants glitch-heavy.

SAFETY, what tools/check_flash.py measures on a 60 fps export scaled to 64x36: general flash = a pair of opposing relative-luminance changes of at least 0.10 (darker state below 0.80) on at least 25 % of pixels; red flash = a pair of opposing changes of at least 20/255 in a saturated-red measure (R / (R+G+B) at least 0.8) on at least 25 % of pixels; pass = no 1 s window with more than 3 flashes of either kind. It also lists single-frame pops (a frame unlike both neighbours while the neighbours are alike), so a one-frame insert is flagged. No measured results are recorded in the README.

SAFETY, current margins and what they allow: the red field #a31b33 has R share 0.68, below the checker's 0.8, so it never counts as saturated red; the section has 9 large-area luminance transitions in 10.8 s, at most 2 in any second (1 flash per second against a limit of 3). At 130 BPM a full-frame flash on every beat is 2.2 per second (inside the limit), on every half-beat 4.3 per second (fails): anything that fires on eighth-notes must stay under 25 % of the frame or under 0.10 luminance change, and stronger light should be reserved for the even beats.
